reasoning: A hybrid approach combines autonomous reasoning to identify baseline patterns in shared features with external XAI tools to quantify feature attribution and validate spuriousness. This ensures both intuitive insight and robust, data-driven evidence of high attribution without semantic relevance.

autonomous_tasks.query: Compare the feature values of instances 541 and 205 across all input columns to identify any overlapping or identical feature values that may indicate a shared spurious pattern.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of feature names that have identical or near-identical values in both instances

autonomous_tasks.query: Assess whether any shared features (e.g., mean smoothness, mean compactness) exhibit values that are outliers or fall in ranges typically associated with class confusion in cancer classification datasets.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: Hypotheses about why the shared features might be spurious and not semantically related to malignant/benign classification

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides consistent, game-theoretic importance scores across instances, allowing us to identify features with high attribution in misclassified cases. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer complementary local and global attribution, helping validate spurious feature influence. Sensitivity analysis isolates feature impact, confirming whether removing a shared feature reduces misclassification probability, thus testing spuriousness.
